text:
I am not so very wise as to deny you,

Lord; I find your divine existence logical;

it is enough for me to open my eyes to find you;

all creation invites me to adore you,

and I adore you in the rose and adore you in the thorn.

What are our anguishes, that we should want to

argue you cruel? Do we perhaps know

if with our tears you make the stars,

if the highest beings, if the most beautiful things

are kneaded with the noble clay of bitterness?

Let us wait, let us suffer, let us never cast

at the Invisible our negation like a challenge.


Poor sad creature, you will see, you will see!

Death draws near... From its lips you will hear

the heavenly secret!

translation.title: I Am Not So Very Wise as to Deny You
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the poem's humble theological logic and its final promise of a secret heard from Death.
